trigger: file.read() blocking on a degraded or network mount (UP-112)

trigger: Any refund that fails to land inside PrincipalQuota::refund

trigger: Transfers being aborted by either deadline

trigger: --ota-transfer-deadline-secs below real transfer time on slow links
summary: A too-short transfer deadline is a SILENT fleet-wide update outage: every transfer aborts, every abort refunds, the agent retries on a 6h timer, so admissions climb, refunds match aborts and RefundDivergence stays quiet - the fleet stops updating and every dashboard is green
classification_rationale: The refund design is what guarantees the silence.

trigger: --ota-max-peers-tracked below the active peer count
summary: Setting max_peers_tracked below the active peer count silently DISABLES the rate dimension: eviction then re-insert mints a full-burst bucket via locate_locked, so every peer arrives with 20 tokens; at =1 the rate limiter is off entirely
classification_rationale: I1 - the rate control does not hold. No warning; _peers_evicted_total is the only tell and has no alert.

BLOCKING (cpp-safety pass 4). Keying the audit limiter on the peer alone left a namespace collision: ota_admission_key reports mode=cert for ANY accepted certificate without consulting the recognizer, so on a multi-CA trust bundle an impostor with a cert from another CA could present CN=<victim agent id>, land in the victim's bucket and suppress the victim's audit rows on demand (I1 - a third party selecting off another principal's forensic attribution). The key now folds in the denial reason, which separates the namespaces: an unrecognised issuer can only provoke foreign_ca. Composed by a pure function (ota_audit_key.hpp). Verified by mutation: removing the reason field reddens 4 assertions across the pure and mTLS suites.

SCOPE DECISION, not a defect. The yuzu-ota alert group is removed from this change and ships separately. Evidence: of 37 findings raised in passes 3-5 against remediation work, 13 were alert-threshold findings - the single largest category - and each was correct, because every threshold is an empirical claim about fleet behaviour with no ground truth in the repo to settle it. Pass 3 proved an absolute bar blind below ~36 agents; pass 4 proved the replacing proportion blind to a permanent 15%-of-fleet outage. That loop terminates on real fleet metrics, not on further review rounds. The METRICS all ship here, with a runbook table giving each one's meaning and first action, so operators can chart them and set local thresholds; only the packaged rules defer.
